1	using Guardrails.Core.Model;
2	
3	namespace Guardrails.Core.Execution;
4	
5	/// <summary>
6	/// Receives progress events as a run proceeds. Keeps the <see cref="Scheduler"/> and
7	/// <see cref="TaskExecutor"/> free of any console/UI dependency; the CLI supplies a
8	/// plain-text or live (Spectre) implementation. Implementations MUST be thread-safe —
9	/// M4 workers emit events concurrently. A no-op default is available via <see cref="Null"/>.
10	/// </summary>
11	public interface IRunObserver
12	{
13	    /// <summary>A task is about to run its action.</summary>
14	    void TaskStarting(TaskNode task);
15	
16	    /// <summary>
17	    /// An attempt is starting: <paramref name="attempt"/> of <paramref name="budget"/>
18	    /// for this run (1-based; budget = 1 + retries).
19	    /// </summary>
20	    void AttemptStarting(TaskNode task, int attempt, int budget) { }
21	
22	    /// <summary>A task finished (succeeded, failed, or was blocked).</summary>
23	    void TaskFinished(TaskResult result);
24	
25	    /// <summary>A guardrail finished running.</summary>
26	    void GuardrailFinished(TaskNode task, GuardrailResult result);
27	
28	    /// <summary>
29	    /// The resumed journal's plan hash differs from the current plan's — the manifests
30	    /// changed since the journal was written. The run continues (SSOT §7); this is a loud
31	    /// warning, not an error.
32	    /// </summary>
33	    void PlanHashMismatch(string previousPlanHash) { }
34	
35	    /// <summary>
36	    /// A plan requested <paramref name="requested"/>-way parallelism but no worktree provider
37	    /// was available, so the scheduler clamped to serial (shared-workspace) execution to avoid
38	    /// an unsafe shared-workspace race (plan 08 §1 / F7). The run continues serially; this is a
39	    /// loud demotion notice, not an error. Default no-op so non-CLI observers need not handle it.
40	    /// </summary>
41	    void ParallelismClampedNoProvider(int requested) { }
42	
43	    /// <summary>
44	    /// A best-effort cleanup operation (a segment-worktree <c>Discard</c> or <c>PruneOrphans</c>)
45	    /// failed during the M2 end-of-run sweep or a failed-task Discard. <paramref name="owner"/> is
46	    /// the owning task id (or a sentinel like <c>(prune-orphans)</c>). The run's verdict is
47	    /// unaffected — a cleanup failure must never flip a green run off-green (plan 08 §D / #126).
48	    /// Default no-op so non-CLI observers need not handle it.
49	    /// </summary>
50	    void CleanupFailed(string owner, Exception error) { }
51	
52	    /// <summary>
53	    /// A task's prompt action hit a TRANSIENT, retryable infrastructure condition (an HTTP 429/503/529,
54	    /// "overloaded", or a usage/session/rate limit) and the harness is PAUSING before re-running the
55	    /// same attempt — WITHOUT consuming the retry budget (SSOT §9, issue #115). <paramref name="reason"/>
56	    /// is the operator-facing cause (carrying a reset hint like "resets 11:20am" when one was present),
57	    /// <paramref name="backoff"/> is how long this pause waits, and <paramref name="pauseCount"/> is the
58	    /// 1-based pause number for this task. A distinct signal so an operator sees a HEALTHY task waiting
59	    /// out a rate limit, not a failing one. Default no-op so non-CLI observers need not handle it.
60	    /// </summary>
61	    void PromptPaused(TaskNode task, string reason, TimeSpan backoff, int pauseCount) { }
62	
63	    /// <summary>An observer that does nothing.</summary>
64	    static IRunObserver Null { get; } = new NullObserver();
65	
66	    private sealed class NullObserver : IRunObserver
67	    {
68	        public void TaskStarting(TaskNode task) { }
69	        public void TaskFinished(TaskResult result) { }
70	        public void GuardrailFinished(TaskNode task, GuardrailResult result) { }
71	        public void PlanHashMismatch(string previousPlanHash) { }
72	    }
73	}
